title: Payroll tax (South Australia)
summary: South Australia taxes employers' wages above a tax-free threshold under the Payroll Tax Act 2009 (SA). Small employers pay nothing; a firm that grows past the threshold starts paying, and exemptions for some employers narrow the base.
direction_rationale: A tax-free threshold works as a tax on growing past it: firms have an incentive to stay below it or to split. e61 found firms bunching just below South Australia's threshold. Exemptions favour some employers over others.

verified.notes: An existing setting: no commencement date is recorded. Thresholds and rates change often and are not recorded here. The site refuses automated requests; the page was found through search results.

review.notes: Drafted by AI-assisted desk research on 28 October 2026 (phase 4 of the productivity framework pivot) from the sources cited. Not yet checked by a person: verify the description, industries and assessment before use.

assessment.summary: A tax on wages above a tax-free threshold. The threshold makes it a tax on growing past a certain size, and exemptions narrow the base; a broad, flat payroll tax would distort less. Firms bunch just below South Australia's threshold.

marks.reason: The threshold is a tax on growing past it, which can hold firms below it.
Thresholds and exemptions make the tax fall unevenly across employers, distorting hiring and firm size.

assessment.confidence_note: Evidence on bunching is mixed: e61 found strong bunching at South Australia's threshold; Treasury found little at most states' thresholds before 2015.
